title: Mahsa Amini Protests
description: Nationwide uprising following the death of Mahsa Amini in morality police custody. Largest protest wave since 1979 revolution, spanning 160+ cities. Security forces killed over 500 protesters.

title: Green Movement Uprising
description: Mass protests erupted after disputed 2009 presidential election. Millions marched in Tehran and other cities demanding annulment of results. Regime crackdown killed dozens and imprisoned hundreds.

title: November 2019 Fuel Price Protests
description: Protests erupted across Iran after government announced sudden 50-300% fuel price hike. Spread to 100+ cities within 48 hours. Internet was shut down nationally for 6 days.

title: December 2017 Economic Protests
description: Spontaneous protests erupted across 80+ Iranian cities over economic hardship, unemployment, and corruption. Chants included 'Death to the dictator' targeting Khamenei directly for the first time. IRGC deployed to suppress protests.

title: 2021 Khuzestan Water Crisis Protests
description: Residents of Khuzestan province took to streets over severe water shortages and mismanagement. At least 8 people killed by security forces. Protests spread to other cities in solidarity with Arab-Iranian minority.

title: Teachers and Workers General Strikes 2018-2019
description: Teachers, truck drivers, sugarcane workers and bazaar merchants staged coordinated nationwide strikes demanding higher wages. Over 1,000 arrested. Strikes marked emergence of organized labor resistance against the regime.

title: 2024 Post-Election Protest Wave
description: Despite nominal election of reformist Pezeshkian, activists documented ongoing street protests over economic conditions and political repression. Civil society groups called for boycotts with lowest-ever turnout in several cities.

title: Mahsa Amini Protest Crackdown - 500+ Killed
description: IRGC and Basij systematically shot protesters across 160+ cities. Amnesty International documented over 500 killed. Thousands imprisoned. Executions of protest-linked detainees followed in 2023.

title: Record 853 Executions in 2023
description: Iran executed at least 853 people in 2023, the highest number in 15 years and one of the highest globally. Many were related to protest convictions under vague national security charges.

title: Bloody November 2019 - Approximately 1500 Killed
description: Security forces killed an estimated 1,500 protesters in six days during the November 2019 uprising according to Reuters citing official sources. The true toll remains unknown due to information blackout.

title: First Executions of Mahsa Amini Protesters
description: Iran executed Mohsen Shekari and Mohammad Mehdi Karami in December 2022 for their role in the protests, the first protest-related executions. International condemnation intensified. Iran pressed ahead with further executions of protesters in 2023.

title: Iran Executions Exceed 700 in 2024
description: Iran surpassed 700 executions by mid-2024, on track for a record year. Death sentences issued under 'Spreading Corruption on Earth' charges against protesters, journalists, and dissidents. UN experts condemned escalation as judicial terror.

title: 2009 Post-Election Torture and Executions
description: Following Green Movement suppression, detainees at Kahrizak detention center were tortured and raped. At least 3 died under torture. Show trials of reformists televised. Dozens executed under national security charges over following years.

title: US Withdrawal from JCPOA Nuclear Deal
description: President Trump announced withdrawal from the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action and reimposed sweeping sanctions. Iran called it a violation of international law. Nuclear deal effectively collapsed.

title: Iran Enriches Uranium to 60% Purity
description: Iran announced it had enriched uranium to 60% purity, a significant step toward weapons-grade 90%. Declared in response to sabotage at Natanz facility. IAEA confirmed the enrichment.

title: Iran Reaches 84% Uranium Enrichment
description: IAEA inspectors detected uranium particles enriched to 84% at Fordow. Iran denied intentional breach, attributing it to technical fluctuations. 84% is near weapons-grade threshold of 90%.

title: Iran Begins Industrial-Scale Uranium Enrichment at Natanz
description: President Ahmadinejad announced Iran had successfully enriched uranium using 164 centrifuges. Defied UN Security Council demands to halt enrichment. Crossed threshold from research to industrial-scale program. International sanctions escalation began.

title: Natanz Advanced Centrifuge Hall Destroyed by Sabotage
description: A major explosion destroyed the advanced centrifuge assembly hall at Natanz facility, widely attributed to Israeli intelligence. Iran accelerated enrichment in response, announcing installation of IR-6 advanced centrifuges 10x faster than IR-1. Triggered direct escalation cycle.

title: Iran Accumulates 128kg of 60% Enriched Uranium
description: IAEA reported Iran had accumulated 128.3 kg of uranium enriched to 60% purity by late 2023, enough for two nuclear weapons if further enriched. With 84% particle detection and monitoring gaps, experts calculated Iran's breakout timeline at under 2 weeks.

title: Iran Installs Advanced IR-6 Centrifuges at Fordow
description: Iran notified IAEA it was installing advanced IR-6 centrifuges at the deeply buried Fordow facility, which is immune to conventional bunker-buster strikes. The move dramatically increased enrichment capacity and signaled Iran was hardening its nuclear sites against military attack.

title: Iran Seizes British Tanker Stena Impero in Strait of Hormuz
description: IRGC Navy commandos fast-roped onto the UK-flagged Stena Impero and seized it in the Strait of Hormuz. UK scrambled warships. Tanker held for 65 days as leverage in diplomatic dispute.

title: Limpet Mine Attacks on Oil Tankers Near Fujairah
description: Multiple oil tankers attacked using limpet mines near the UAE port of Fujairah. US and Saudi Arabia attributed attacks to Iran. Two tankers severely damaged. Created global maritime insurance crisis.

title: Iranian-Backed Houthi Attacks on Red Sea Shipping
description: Yemen-based Houthis, armed and directed by Iran, launched sustained drone and missile attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea. Forced major shipping rerouting around Cape of Good Hope. Significant global supply chain disruption.

title: Iran Drone Attack Kills Security Guard on MV Mercer Street
description: A one-way attack drone struck the Israeli-managed tanker MV Mercer Street in the Gulf of Oman, killing a British and Romanian crew member. US, UK, and Israel attributed the attack to Iran. First Iran drone attack to kill Western nationals on a commercial vessel.

title: IRGC Seizes MSC Aries Container Ship in Strait of Hormuz
description: IRGC commandos rappelled from a helicopter to seize the MSC Aries, a Portugal-flagged container ship with 25 crew, in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran held the vessel for months. Marked the largest commercial vessel seizure by Iran and directly threatened global container shipping.

title: IRGC Boats Attempt to Board HMS Montrose
description: IRGC patrol boats attempted to intercept and board the British-flagged Heritage oil tanker but were warned off by HMS Montrose. Iran denied the incident. Occurred during peak Hormuz tensions. Escalated naval confrontation in the world's most critical oil chokepoint.

title: Iran Mines Gulf Waters, Disrupts Global Oil Flows
description: Iran deployed naval mines in the Persian Gulf region as part of a gray-zone pressure campaign. CENTCOM tracked increased IRGC mine-laying activities near international shipping lanes. Disrupted 20% of world oil transit through Hormuz.

title: Stuxnet Worm Destroys Natanz Centrifuges
description: The Stuxnet cyberweapon, widely attributed to US-Israeli intelligence, physically destroyed approximately 1,000 Iranian uranium enrichment centrifuges at Natanz. First known cyberweapon to cause physical destruction.

title: Cyberattack Paralyzes Iranian Fuel Distribution Network
description: A major cyberattack, attributed to Israel-linked group Predatory Sparrow, took down Iran's national fuel distribution network. Over 4,300 petrol stations went offline. Regime accused of cover-up.

title: Shamoon Malware Destroys 30,000 Saudi Aramco Workstations
description: Iran-linked hackers deployed the Shamoon malware against Saudi Aramco, destroying 30,000 computer workstations in hours. Most destructive cyberattack on a private company in history at the time. Demonstrated Iran's willingness to conduct destructive cyber operations against critical infrastructure.

title: US DOJ Indicts Iranian Hackers for Power Grid and Dam Attacks
description: US Justice Department indicted Iranian hackers for targeting US power grids, water systems, and a New York dam control system. Iranian APT groups also breached networks of US financial institutions. First indictment explicitly naming IRGC-linked hackers for attacks on critical infrastructure.

title: Iran APT MuddyWater Compromises US Federal Networks
description: CISA and FBI issued joint alert that Iranian state-sponsored MuddyWater group actively targeted US, UK, and European government networks. Campaigns focused on espionage and pre-positioning for destructive attacks. Over 50 US government agencies affected.

title: Iran Escalates Cyber Operations Against US and Israel in 2024
description: CISA and NSA documented a surge in Iranian cyber operations targeting US defense contractors, Israeli water infrastructure, and Albanian government systems. IRGC Cyber Command expanded its offensive toolkit with custom wiper malware. Election interference operations also documented.

title: Gonjeshke Darande Attacks Iran Steel Plants and Rail Network
description: Hacktivist group Gonjeshke Darande, linked to Israeli intelligence, disrupted operations at three Iranian steel plants and Iran's national rail system. Steel plant attacks caused fires visible on satellite imagery. First known destructive attack on Iranian heavy industry.

title: US Drone Strike Assassinates IRGC General Qasem Soleimani
description: US airstrike at Baghdad airport killed IRGC Quds Force commander Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi PMF commander Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. Most significant direct US-Iran military action in decades. Iran vowed revenge.

title: Iran Fires 16 Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Iraq
description: Iran launched 16 ballistic missiles at Al-Assad and Erbil air bases in Iraq hosting US forces. First direct Iranian state-on-state ballistic missile attack on US military. Over 100 US personnel suffered traumatic brain injuries.

title: Iran Launches Operation True Promise I - 300 Drones and Missiles at Israel
description: Iran launched over 300 drones and missiles directly at Israel from Iranian soil, the first direct state-on-state attack between Iran and Israel. Over 99% intercepted by US, UK, French, Jordanian, and Israeli forces. Marked historic escalation.

title: Hezbollah-Israel War 2006 - Iran Proves Proxy Deterrence
description: Hezbollah, armed and funded by Iran's IRGC, fought Israel to a military stalemate in 34 days. Hezbollah fired over 4,000 rockets into Israel, including precision-guided missiles supplied by Iran. Demonstrated Iran's ability to project military deterrence through proxies without direct exposure.

title: Iran Shoots Down US RQ-4A Global Hawk Surveillance Drone
description: Iran's IRGC shot down a US Navy RQ-4A Global Hawk drone worth $220 million over the Strait of Hormuz using a surface-to-air missile. US disputed Iran's claim it was in Iranian airspace. President Trump initially authorized retaliatory strikes before canceling minutes before launch.

title: Iran Launches Operation True Promise II - 200 Ballistic Missiles at Israel
description: Iran fired approximately 200 ballistic missiles at Israel in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Iranian territory. Several missiles impacted Israeli military bases including Nevatim Air Base. Israel vowed direct retaliation. Represented the most significant conventional ballistic missile barrage in modern warfare history.

title: Hardliner Ebrahim Raisi Wins Presidential Election
description: Ebrahim Raisi, linked to the 1988 mass executions of political prisoners, won Iran's presidential election after reformist candidates were disqualified. Lowest voter turnout in Islamic Republic history. Marked consolidation of hardliner control.

title: IAEA Board Censures Iran, Cuts Monitoring Access
description: IAEA Board of Governors voted to censure Iran for lack of cooperation. Iran responded by disconnecting 27 IAEA monitoring cameras, creating a massive intelligence blind spot on nuclear activities.

title: Ahmadinejad Elected, Declares Nuclear Defiance
description: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad won Iran's presidency on platform of anti-Western defiance. Declared Iran would never abandon its nuclear program regardless of UN pressure. Ended diplomatic opening of Khatami era. Set Iran on confrontational path that led to maximum sanctions regime.

title: JCPOA Revival Talks Collapse Under Raisi Government
description: Negotiations to revive the 2015 nuclear deal broke down after Iran demanded removal of IRGC from US terror list and guarantees no future president could leave. US walked away from near-final deal in August 2022. Diplomatic path to resolving nuclear crisis closed.

title: President Raisi Killed in Helicopter Crash, Hardliner Succession Secured
description: President Raisi and Foreign Minister Amir-Abdollahian died in helicopter crash in fog-shrouded mountains. Khamenei declared 5 days of mourning. Despite nominal election of reformist Pezeshkian, hardliners retained full control of IRGC, judiciary, and parliament. Khamenei's succession dynamics accelerated.

title: Iran-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
description: Iran and Russia signed a 20-year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership covering defense, energy, trade, and technology. Iran supplied Russia with Shahed drones and ballistic missiles for use in Ukraine. Russia provided advanced air defense systems and Su-35 jets to Iran. New axis fundamentally altered regional power balance.

title: Khamenei Signals Nuclear Doctrine Shift, Fatwa Under Review
description: Senior IRGC commanders and regime ideologists publicly floated reversing Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons. State media carried analyses arguing weapons capability was now religiously permissible given existential threats. Intelligence assessments indicated Iran was within weeks of weapons-grade material.

title: Iranian Rial Collapses 80% Under Sanctions
description: The Iranian rial lost approximately 80% of its value as US and EU sanctions tightened. Oil exports halved. Imports of medicine and basic goods severely disrupted. Middle class wealth effectively destroyed.

title: Iran Annual Inflation Exceeds 40% Under Maximum Pressure
description: Following US maximum pressure campaign sanctions, Iran's annual inflation rate exceeded 40% with food inflation reaching 60%+. Unemployment and poverty rates surged. IMF cited as among world's worst economic contractions.

title: Iranian Rial Hits Historic Low, 600,000 per USD
description: The Iranian rial reached a new historic low of approximately 600,000 rials per US dollar in 2023, compared to 32,000 per dollar in 2011. Purchasing power of ordinary Iranians collapsed. Black market premiums widespread.

title: Iran Oil Exports Collapse to Near Zero Under Maximum Pressure
description: US maximum pressure sanctions reduced Iran's oil exports from 2.5 million barrels/day to under 300,000 bpd by mid-2019. Lost approximately $200 billion in oil revenues over four years. Budget deficit forced withdrawal from sovereign wealth funds and social program cuts.

title: 60% of Iranians Living Below Poverty Line by 2023
description: Iranian parliamentary research center reported 60% of Iranians living below the absolute poverty line by 2023, up from 25% in 2010. Youth unemployment above 25%. Brain drain accelerated with 150,000+ skilled professionals emigrating annually. UN identified structural collapse in social safety net.

title: Iran 2022 Budget Deficit Crisis and Currency Collapse
description: Iran's 2022 budget was based on oil price assumptions 60% above actual export revenues, creating structural deficit. Government resorted to printing money, accelerating inflation to 52%. Foreign exchange reserves fell to levels insufficient to cover 3 months of imports.

title: Operation Epic Fury: US-Israel Launch 900 Strikes Against Iran in 12 Hours
description: US and Israeli forces launched nearly 900 joint strikes in the first 12 hours of Operation Epic Fury on February 28, 2026, targeting Iranian missile arsenals, air defense systems, IRGC military infrastructure, leadership compounds, and nuclear program sites. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in an Israeli air strike. Operation ran from February 28 to May 5, 2026.

title: Iran Operation True Promise IV: Retaliates Across 7 Countries
description: Iran launched Operation True Promise IV in immediate retaliation for Operation Epic Fury, extending the war's geographic footprint to Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Iraq within 48 hours. Ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones struck US military installations and allied infrastructure across the region.

title: Iran Breaks April Ceasefire, Fires 30 Ballistic Missiles at Israel
description: Iran broke the Pakistan-brokered April 8 ceasefire by firing approximately 30 ballistic missiles at northern Israel on June 6-8, 2026, in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Beirut. First direct Iranian missile attack since the ceasefire. Trump warned Netanyahu 'you'll be on your own' if attacks on Iran continue. Israel and Iran paused operations following the exchange.

title: Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei Assassinated in Israeli Air Strike
description: Ali Khamenei, Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic since 1989, was killed in an Israeli air strike on February 28, 2026, as part of Operation Epic Fury. Iranian state media announced his death on March 1. His daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law were also killed. Eliminated the singular authority figure of the Islamic Republic and triggered acute succession crisis.

title: Ceasefire Collapses, Trump-Netanyahu Rift, Negotiations Stalled
description: The April 8 ceasefire collapsed in early June 2026 as Israel resumed strikes on Beirut and Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles. Trump reportedly called Netanyahu 'f***ing crazy' during a phone call and warned he would be 'on your own.' Iran's Foreign Minister said no significant progress in negotiations. Pakistan brokering further talks with no agreement.

title: US-Israel Strikes Destroy Iran Nuclear Infrastructure at Natanz, Fordow, Parchin
description: Operation Epic Fury specifically targeted Iran's nuclear infrastructure including the Natanz enrichment facility, the deeply buried Fordow site, the Parchin explosive research facility, and the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran headquarters. Despite extensive damage, Iran retains approximately 400 kg of 60% enriched uranium whose location remains unknown, creating acute proliferation risk.

title: Nationwide Protests Erupt Across Iran — Largest Since 1979 Revolution
description: Sparked by economic collapse and currency freefall, mass protests began December 28, 2025, spreading to over 200 cities within days. Reza Pahlavi called for coordinated simultaneous protests at 8:00 PM on January 8-9, 2026. Millions responded. The protests quickly became explicitly anti-regime, calling for an end to the Islamic Republic. Security forces and internet shutdowns failed to contain the uprising, setting the stage for the January massacre.

title: Iran Mass Executions and Arrests During War Footing
description: Iran's judiciary accelerated executions of political prisoners, dissidents, and protest-linked detainees during the war period, framing them as 'traitors collaborating with the enemy.' IRGC conducted sweeping arrests of civil society figures, journalists, and dual nationals. International monitors documented dozens of executions under 'spreading corruption' charges.

title: Iran Threatens Strait of Hormuz Closure, Naval Skirmishes Erupt
description: IRGC Navy conducted aggressive maneuvers and threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz during Operation Epic Fury. Deployed fast attack boats and submarines. Oil prices spiked over 80% within days. Multiple naval skirmishes with US 5th Fleet. Iran briefly seized two oil tankers before being forced to release them under US naval pressure.

title: Iran Oil Production Collapses Under War, Global Oil Spikes 80%
description: Operation Epic Fury strikes targeted Iranian oil infrastructure, effectively halting exports. Oil prices spiked over 80% globally within days, threatening recession. Iran's budget, already in crisis, collapsed entirely. IMF projected Iran's GDP to contract 35% in 2026. Barter economy emerged in major cities as banking system froze under maximum sanctions.

title: IRGC Cyber Units Launch Unprecedented Attacks on US Infrastructure During War
description: Iranian IRGC cyber units launched the largest coordinated cyberattack campaign in history against US critical infrastructure during Operation Epic Fury, targeting power grids, water systems, financial networks, and hospital systems. CISA issued emergency directives. Several US power utilities reported outages. FBI attributed attacks to IRGC Cyber Command and its civilian contractors.

title: US and Israel Discuss Special Forces Raid to Seize Iran's Nuclear Uranium Stockpile
description: Axios (March 8) and CNN (March 9, 2026) reported that US and Israeli officials were actively discussing deploying special forces into Iran to secure and seize an estimated 400 kg of 60%-enriched uranium believed to be stored in underground tunnels at Isfahan — tunnels too deep for conventional airstrikes. Capturing the stockpile would require a significant ground force beyond a small special operations footprint. The White House said ground operations are 'not part of the plan right now' but Trump was keeping options open. The discussions reflect active US planning for physical control of Iran's nuclear material in a post-regime-collapse scenario.

title: Reza Pahlavi Publishes Detailed Emergency Transition Plan for Post-Regime Iran
description: On January 6, 2026, Reza Pahlavi published an op-ed in The Washington Post titled 'Iran is ready for a democratic transition,' accompanied by a detailed Emergency Phase governance blueprint. The plan designates Pahlavi as 'Leader of the National Uprising' with authority to form a transitional Mehestan (legislature), transitional government, and transitional Divan (judiciary). It calls for the immediate abolition of the Supreme Leader office, Assembly of Experts, Guardian Council, and Expediency Council, and the dissolution of the IRGC. This is the first time an Iranian opposition leader has published a functioning government-in-waiting with institutional structure, international recognition, and US-Israeli diplomatic backing simultaneously.

title: IRGC Military Council Stages Silent Coup, Seizes All State Functions
description: By April 2026, Iran's IRGC had formed an unelected military council of senior officers that seized effective control of all state functions, operating entirely outside Iran's theocratic constitution. The IRGC blocked all presidential appointments, with IRGC chief-commander Ahmad Vahidi rejecting every candidate for intelligence minister proposed by President Pezeshkian. The military council — answering to no elected official — began making all key governance decisions. Iran International reported the IRGC was no longer operating behind the scenes but openly emerging as the sole governing authority. PJ Media noted the war had 'shattered the Iranian leadership structure, making an agreement next to impossible.'

title: Iranian President Pezeshkian Offers Resignation Over IRGC Coup
description: On May 31, 2026, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian submitted an official letter of resignation to the Office of the Supreme Leader, stating that the IRGC had seized control and cut him out of all decisions. His office subsequently denied the report, but Iran International and multiple sources confirmed the resignation letter's existence. Pezeshkian, elected in 2025 on a moderate reform platform, found himself with no authority under the IRGC military council. The incident marks the complete collapse of civilian government in the Islamic Republic — the presidency has been rendered a ceremonial position under military occupation of state functions.

title: US Launches Second Wave of Strikes on Multiple Targets in Southern Iran
description: US Central Command launched a second consecutive day of strikes on 'multiple targets in Iran' on June 9-10, 2026, citing Iran's 'unwarranted and continued aggression.' A GBU-39 precision-guided munition struck water reservoirs in the Bamani district of southern Iran, destroying two concrete reservoirs serving over 20,000 civilians. The strikes came after Iran downed a US Army attack helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump and Defense Secretary Hegseth had warned Tehran of severe consequences. War's 100th-day milestone passed amid active escalation.

title: Iran Shoots Down US Army Attack Helicopter Near Strait of Hormuz
description: An Iranian drone collided with a US Army attack helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz on June 9, 2026, causing it to crash. US officials confirmed the downing. CENTCOM said the attack triggered the new wave of US strikes on Iran. The incident demonstrated Iran retains operational drone capability to threaten US military assets in the world's most critical oil chokepoint even as the broader war continues.

title: Southern Iran Strikes Deepen Economic Collapse, Global Oil Markets Rocked
description: US precision strikes on southern Iranian infrastructure on June 9-10, 2026, including water and industrial facilities in Hormuz province, compounded Iran's already catastrophic wartime economic collapse. Iranian GDP contraction projections were revised upward. Global oil markets responded with further price spikes as Hormuz traffic disruption intensified. Iran's banking system remained frozen under maximum sanctions with no functioning SWIFT access.

title: JCPOA Nuclear Agreement Signed — Iran Accepts Enrichment Limits
description: Iran and the P5+1 (US, UK, France, Germany, Russia, China) signed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action on July 14, 2015. Iran agreed to cap uranium enrichment at 3.67%, reduce its centrifuge count by two-thirds, redesign the Arak reactor to prevent weapons-grade plutonium production, and accept intrusive IAEA monitoring. In exchange, most international sanctions were lifted. For approximately three years the deal froze Iran's nuclear program at sub-weapons-grade levels and restored IAEA camera access to all declared sites.

title: Iran Receives Sanctions Relief Under JCPOA — Oil Exports Partially Restored
description: Following JCPOA implementation in January 2016, the EU and US lifted nuclear-related sanctions. Iran's oil exports rose from under 1 million bpd to approximately 2.5 million bpd by mid-2017. The rial briefly stabilized, inflation fell from 40% to under 10%, and GDP grew 12.5% in 2016 (IMF). The partial economic normalization lasted until the US reimposed sanctions in May 2018 following Trump's JCPOA withdrawal.

title: Pakistan-Brokered Ceasefire Halts Active US-Iran-Israel Hostilities
description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif brokered a ceasefire agreement on April 8, 2026, halting active US-Iran-Israel hostilities after 38 days of Operation Epic Fury. Iran agreed to freeze offensive missile launches; the US paused strikes on Iranian territory; Israel suspended strikes on Iranian territory pending parallel Lebanon negotiations. The ceasefire held through late May before collapsing when Israel resumed strikes on Beirut and Iran retaliated with 30 ballistic missiles on June 6-8, 2026.

title: Israel Assassinates Ali Larijani — Iran's De Facto Post-Khamenei Leader
description: On March 17, 2026, Israel assassinated Ali Larijani, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, in an airstrike on the outskirts of eastern Tehran. His son Morteza and the head of his office Alireza Bayat were also killed. Larijani had been appointed by President Pezeshkian in August 2025 and was widely described by international media as the most powerful man in Iran and its de facto leader after Khamenei's assassination. On the same night, Basij commander Gholamreza Soleimani was killed in a separate Israeli airstrike. The back-to-back eliminations — Khamenei (Feb 28) and Larijani (Mar 17) — decapitated Iran's two most senior leadership figures within 17 days, leaving the IRGC military council as the only functioning authority.

title: Iran Formally Closes Strait of Hormuz to All Shipping — Day 104 of War
description: On June 11, 2026 (Day 104 of the war), Iran's joint military command formally declared the complete closure of the Strait of Hormuz to all oil tankers and commercial ships, stating that any vessel attempting passage would be shot at. The closure came in direct response to the US firing 49 Tomahawk missiles at Iranian targets including military surveillance systems, communications, and air defense sites, with explosions reported in Tehran suburbs, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, and Kharg Island. Since February 28, Iran had been intermittently allowing passage for fees reportedly as high as $2 million per vessel. The formal permanent closure blockades 20% of global oil and LNG supply, the single largest disruption to global energy markets in modern history. Iran's IRGC also claimed attacks on US military bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan in response.

title: US Fires 49 Tomahawk Missiles at Iran; Iran Attacks US Bases Across Four Countries
description: On June 11, 2026, US Central Command fired 49 Tomahawk cruise missiles at Iranian military targets including surveillance systems, communication networks, and air defense sites. Explosions were reported in Tehran suburbs (Abyek, Qarchak, Nazarabad, Karaj), Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, and Kharg Island. In retaliation, Iran's IRGC claimed strikes against US military installations in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. The exchange marked the single most intense day of direct US-Iran kinetic combat since Operation Epic Fury began. Trump had warned earlier in the day that he would hit Iran 'VERY HARD' and threatened to seize Iran's oil and gas sectors.

title: Trump Cancels Planned Iran Strikes, Claims Deal 'Approved' — Iran Denies
description: Hours after vowing to hit Iran 'VERY HARD,' President Trump abruptly canceled military strikes planned for the evening of June 11, 2026, claiming that 'discussions have been brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership' and that a deal's 'time and place of signing will be announced shortly.' Stock markets soared and oil prices fell sharply on the announcement. However, Iranian state media reported that Tehran had not approved any text for an initial memorandum of understanding, and Iranian officials stated they viewed any negotiations as a continuation of the battlefield. Multiple analysts noted Trump had made similar claims of an imminent deal in March and May with no agreement emerging. The episode represents a genuine but contested de-escalation signal — the first time the US has canceled a scheduled military operation against Iran since the war began.

title: Khamenei Orders Massacre of Protesters — 30,000–40,000 Killed in Two Days
description: On January 9, 2026, Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei ordered security forces to kill protesters and show no mercy. Over January 8–9, IRGC and Basij forces opened fire on crowds across Iran, killing an estimated 30,000–36,500 people in two days according to The Guardian, Time, and Iran International citing local health officials. HRANA confirmed over 7,000 deaths with 11,744 additional cases under review. The massacre was the deadliest state violence in Iran since the 1988 prison executions. Rather than ending the opposition, the slaughter galvanized Reza Pahlavi's international campaign to bring US and Israeli military intervention, directly preceding Operation Epic Fury.

title: Regime Hardliners Protest in Tehran Against US Deal: 'Why Negotiate With Khamenei's Killers?'
description: Hundreds of IRGC-aligned hardliners, Basij members, and regime loyalists staged demonstrations in Tehran on June 12, 2026, against the Iranian government's ongoing nuclear negotiations with the United States. Protesters chanted 'Why are you negotiating with the killers of our Supreme Leader?' and 'Death to the Deal.' The protests reflect a deep rift within the regime itself: pragmatic IRGC commanders seeking an exit from the war through diplomacy versus hardline ideologues who view any deal as a betrayal of Khamenei's legacy. Iran International noted that hardliners 'want to kill the deal.' The internal protest movement signals that even if IRGC leadership signs an agreement, it will face organized resistance from within the regime's own support base — a historically destabilizing dynamic.

title: Trump: Iran Deal to Be Signed This Sunday; Pakistan PM Confirms 'Final Agreed Text'
description: On June 12, 2026, President Trump announced the US-Iran peace deal would be signed 'this Sunday' (June 14-15) at a European venue with VP JD Vance attending. Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif, acting as mediator, confirmed a 'final, agreed upon text' had been reached. A senior US official estimated 80-85% confidence the deal would be signed, noting Iran's system is 'very complicated.' The deal would formalize a ceasefire, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch 60 days of formal nuclear negotiations. Trump had previously made similar claims in March and May with no agreement emerging, but Pakistan's direct third-party confirmation distinguishes this episode from prior false starts.

title: Iran Foreign Ministry: Deal Reports 'Mere Speculation,' No Final Decision Made
description: Hours after Trump announced a deal this Sunday, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told state media that reports of a finalized agreement were 'mere speculation' and Tehran had made 'no final decision on any deal.' Baghaei stated the US 'repeatedly changed its positions during talks.' The statement directly contradicted Pakistan's PM Sharif. The contradiction between Trump/Pakistan and Iran's Foreign Ministry reflects genuine internal disagreement within Iran: IRGC commanders in the negotiating channel willing to deal versus hardline political figures who view any agreement as capitulation to the forces that killed Khamenei. A state unable to speak with one voice on an existential war-ending decision is institutionally fractured.

title: US-Iran Deal Framework: Iran to Surrender Enriched Uranium and Dismantle Nuclear Program
description: According to US officials and Pakistan's mediation team, the tentative MoU finalized June 12, 2026 would require Iran to: surrender all highly enriched uranium above 5% (including the contested 400kg of 60%-enriched stockpile) to the United States; shut down and dismantle remaining centrifuge networks; accept immediate continuous IAEA inspection access; and enter 60 days of binding nuclear negotiations. The terms exceed the 2015 JCPOA in scope — effectively ending Iran's nuclear program under US-supervised dismantlement. Iran's Foreign Ministry formally denied any final text exists. If verified and signed, this would represent the largest nuclear concession by any state since Libya's 2003 disarmament. The contested status means this is a partial de-escalation signal pending confirmation.

title: IRGC Rejects Sunday Deal Timeline; Iran FM Says Signing 'Not Tomorrow'
description: On June 13, 2026, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued a statement criticizing President Trump's 'unusual insistence' on a Sunday signing date for the peace deal, warning that the tight timeline risked derailing negotiations. Hours later, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated that the signing 'will not be tomorrow' but that 'the possibility it will happen in the coming days is not ruled out.' Officials confirmed that a virtual signing was being planned because an in-person meeting presented logistical challenges. The dual statements reflect the structural fracture in Iran's negotiating chain: IRGC commanders willing to deal on military terms versus political and ideological figures viewing any agreement as capitulation. Qatar dispatched negotiators to Tehran in a last-minute push to finalize the text.

title: Trump Declares 'Deal with Iran Now Complete' — Islamabad Declaration Announced
description: On June 14, 2026, President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'The Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete.' Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif made a parallel announcement minutes before Trump's statement, and Iranian state media broadcast the declaration. The Islamabad Declaration commits both sides to an immediate and permanent cessation of war on all fronts, including in Lebanon, and prohibits either party from initiating future hostilities. Immediately after signing, the US will begin lifting its maritime blockade, with Hormuz reaching full commercial capacity within 30 days. Iran and the US will hold negotiations and reach a final agreement within 60 days. The agreement represents the first formal termination of active hostilities since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28, 2026 — 107 days earlier.

title: Strait of Hormuz to Reopen; US Naval Blockade Lifted Under Islamabad Declaration
description: A core term of the June 14 Islamabad Declaration commits Iran to immediately open the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping while the United States simultaneously lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports. The US commits to bringing Hormuz shipping to full commercial capacity within a maximum of 30 days. Iran's formal closure of the Strait on June 11 — with a shoot-on-sight order for any transiting vessel — had constituted the single largest deliberate disruption of global energy markets in modern history, blocking 20% of global oil and LNG supply. The reopening requires Iran's joint military command to stand down from active maritime interdiction. Full implementation is contingent on both governments ratifying the Islamabad Declaration.

title: Iran Commits to 'Never Acquire Nuclear Weapons'; 440kg Stockpile Stays in Tehran During 60-Day Talks
description: The Islamabad Declaration's nuclear annex commits Iran to never acquiring a nuclear weapon and initiates a 60-day negotiation period on the full disposition of Iran's nuclear program, including suspension of uranium enrichment and the eventual removal of its highly enriched uranium stockpile. However, a critical limitation confirmed by the Axios draft text and official US and Iranian statements: Iran's existing 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60 percent purity — a level the IAEA has flagged as having no credible civilian justification — remains in Tehran's possession throughout the entire 60-day period. The MoU names no verification mechanism, inspection protocol, or requirement to move or secure the enriched material before signing. This means the weapons-material proliferation risk persists unmitigated throughout the negotiation window.

title: Iran and US Hold Contradictory Versions of Islamabad Declaration Text
description: Fortune reported on June 14, 2026, that Iran and the United States were promoting fundamentally different versions of the Islamabad Declaration. The Persian-language draft circulated inside Iran differed significantly from the English version presented by the US side on key provisions: sanctions lifting terms (Iran's draft required full lifting; US draft staged relief by compliance milestone), the geographic scope of the ceasefire commitment, the mechanism for verifying Iran's nuclear freeze, and the threshold conditions under which the 60-day negotiation window would be considered to have failed. Iranian officials described the MoU as a 'declaration of intent' rather than a binding agreement, while US officials characterized it as a 'signed framework.' The divergence suggests both parties agreed to sign structurally different documents to satisfy domestic audiences — a pattern historically associated with high-probability framework collapse within the agreed negotiation window.
